transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Recording ID: ff-2025-08-12-helix-001
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM); Ethan Morales (Helix PM), Priya Singh (Helix ML Lead), Laura Kim (Helix CTO)

Auto-summary: quick sync to triage recent regression in hallucination rates on the pilot, compare per-prompt scoring, discuss guardrail tuning and next evals.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay, uh good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I see folks on the call. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Ethan Morales: Ethan here, PM for the Helix pilot, mm-hmm.
[00:11] Priya Singh: Priya, ML.
[00:12] Laura Kim: Laura, CTO, I'm on.
[00:15] Daniel Park: Daniel from Redwood, SE.
[00:17] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, CSM.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda: look at the latest scorecard, dig into the 2.2x uptick in false positives on assay parsing, propose guardrail tweaks, and decide whether we need a dedicated dev pool for the next set of runs.

[02:05] Priya Singh: Quick background — since last week our end-to-end metric for structured extraction dropped from 92 to about 86, and the hallucination-ish class, like where the model invents reagent concentrations, increased. We re-ran the base prompts and saw the change across variants.

[03:00] Maya Chen: Thanks Priya. Did you pin the model version used? Was it the redwood-1-large or the open checkpoint?
[03:10] Priya Singh: It's redwood-1-large-v3, but we also had a fallback to r1-small for long tails. There might be some routing flips during peaks.

[03:40] Daniel Park: We saw a routing fallback flagged in our logs around 02:30 PT — that caused some requests to go to the quantized variant which has a slightly different tokenizer behavior, so that could explain drift.
[04:01] Ethan Morales: Uh mmm, okay so two things — routing and prompt drift. For the scorecard itself, can we look at per-prompt breakdown?
[04:10] Sofia Alvarez: I've uploaded the latest scorecard to the shared drive — link in the CRM notes — filename: helix_pilot_scorecard_2025-08-12.csv.
[04:40] [05:00] Screen share referenced (not recorded in transcript)
[05:12] Priya Singh: On prompt set A1 we see recall drop, on A3 precision drops — looks like some prompts are more sensitive to sequence length, likely because of KV cache misses or truncation.
[05:34] Daniel Park: yeah, the KV cache, or as sometimes the transcription says "K V cache" — if the caching windows misalign we see prefix tokens re-generated. Also the quantized kernel has slightly higher repetition probability on longer contexts.
[06:10] Laura Kim: Is that something that is a function of our average request size? We do have some long clinical notes in some of the test records.
[06:20] Priya Singh: Average sequence length is 1.4k tokens for the sample set. Some edge cases hit 3k.
[06:28] Maya Chen: Ok, so two levers: first keep the non-quantized variant for the sensitive prompts, second tune guardrails to detect spurious concentrations. Daniel, did you prototype a guardrail rule?
[06:40] Daniel Park: Yep — I prototyped two heuristics: one is a regex-plus-constraint that flags concentration mentions outside plausible ranges, and the other is a content-similarity check against known reagent lists. The heuristic combined with a thresholded semantic check reduced hallucination signals in internal runs by ~60%. Note: internal runs were on a dev pool with consistent kernel selection.
[07:20] Ethan Morales: That sounds promising. How do false negatives behave — do we start suppressing valid but rare concentrations?
[07:30] Daniel Park: There's a tradeoff — the rule is tunable. We can add an allow-list for verified reagents and lower the severity for unknowns, then route those to a higher-precision model instead of blocking them.
[07:50] Priya Singh: We'd prefer reroute to a higher-precision runner than outright suppression, because for the product team missing a result is worse.
[08:05] Maya Chen: Good. So proposed flow: heuristic flag -> allow-list check -> if unknown, route to dedicated non-quantized variant with higher temperature control and stricter decoding. If still low confidence, raise to human review.
[08:25] Laura Kim: Sounds good. How much overhead does that routing add?
[08:32] Daniel Park: Latency adds ~110-180ms on average for rerouted requests in our infra; cost is about 1.8x for those tokens because of the higher-precision runner. But given the low percentage of flagged cases it's manageable.
[09:00] [09:15] Ethan Morales: On the scorecard, we noticed some regression specifically tied to prompt variant B — the one with more free-text guidance. Any insight?
[09:25] Daniel Park: free-text guidance can increase variance — when prompts are long the model hallucinates reconciling instructions with noisy context. For B we saw a lot of stray reagent names injected. We can shorten directive text and move examples to structured bulleted sections.
[09:54] Priya Singh: We'll try a condensed version and keep the example set separate. I'll update the prompt set and push to the shared bucket.
[10:08] Sofia Alvarez: Quick note: I saw in the logs an SSO error for one of your dev users — Sam L authentication failed — that's probably SAML misconfig on Helix side.
[10:20] Laura Kim: Yeah we changed the cert last week, will check.
[10:25] Maya Chen: Noted. Not critical to the pilot runs but good to fix.
[10:40] [11:10] Discussion: scoring thresholds and evaluation harness
[11:25] Daniel Park: For the eval harness we recommend two additional runs: 1) guardrail-on baseline (no quantization), 2) guardrail-on + reroute-to-high-precision for flagged cases, and 3) guardrail with relaxed allow-list to estimate FN risk. We'll export per-prompt and per-example scores.
[12:00] Priya Singh: For metrics we want: per-prompt precision/recall/F1, hallucination-rate (measured as extraneous numeric entries), and a per-example confidence score distribution.
[12:20] Maya Chen: We'll include an ensemble delta column to show improvement vs the current baseline.
[12:30] Ethan Morales: One more ask: can we get example-level traces (the token log) for 25 failures so we can see the KV cache behavior?
[12:39] Daniel Park: Yes, we can. I'll export token traces but note that token traces are large, so we'll share 25 samples compressed in a ZIP in the drive.
[12:55] Priya Singh: Also please annotate which runs used quantized kernels vs full precision, because that mattered.
[13:05] Daniel Park: will do. We'll label them redwood-1-large-v3-quant and redwood-1-large-v3-full.
[13:18] [13:40] Discussion: guardrail false positives and tuning strategy
[13:50] Maya Chen: Priya, can you describe the failure modes you're most worried about?
[13:55] Priya Singh: Sure — 1) invented concentrations (e.g., "0.34 mg/ml" when none in source), 2) swapped reagent names across lines, 3) extra steps appended that didn't exist. The first is the most frequent.
[14:18] Daniel Park: For 1) our heuristics detect numeric patterns and cross-check against context; for 2) we can boost alignment constraints by including position-aware prompts; for 3) we can add a post-parse trimming step that enforces step counts.
[14:40] Ethan Morales: Sounds engineering heavy — what's the effort estimate?
[14:45] Daniel Park: Guardrail heuristics are low to medium effort — a few days for the initial rules and another week to tune thresholds. Reroute policies and allow-lists are config changes.
[15:05] Sofia Alvarez: I'll put a timeline in the scorecard doc.
[15:20] [15:40] Noise / crosstalk for a few seconds, then resumes
[16:00] Laura Kim: One compliance item — are logs and traces meeting our audit needs? We need redacted audit logs with KMS integration.
[16:10] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log retention policies. For the hosted pilot we can provide pseudo-redacted traces; for enterprise we can set up VPC Private deployment.
[16:28] Laura Kim: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
[16:32] Daniel Park: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. We can share the compliance pack linked in the CRM.
[16:45] Priya Singh: Ok that's good. Data residency — we need EU-only for a subset of records.
[16:51] Maya Chen: We can region pin those requests to eu-west-1 — config change. We'll document in run plan.
[17:05] [17:20] Discussion: pilot economics and dedicated dev pool
[17:30] Ethan Morales: If we end up routing 4% of requests to the higher-precision runner, what's the delta on monthly cost?
[17:38] Daniel Park: Back-of-envelope: overall tokens cost +25% on those routed tokens; at 4% of total request volume that's roughly +1% overall spend. We can run a cost projection and put numbers in the deck.
[17:55] Maya Chen: If results are promising Helix might want to move to a small dedicated dev pool to stabilize kernel selection; that would also fix routing the issue.
[18:08] Priya Singh: OK let's keep that as an outcome condition — if guardrail + reroute reduces hallucinations by >50% we consider dedicated dev pool.
[18:20] Maya Chen: Agreed.
[18:30] [18:45] Quick recap and next steps
[18:50] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to run three evals (guardrail-off baseline, guardrail-on with reroute, guardrail-on relaxed allow-list), export per-prompt CSV + 25 token traces; Helix to upload 200 labeled edge samples; timeframe target mid-next-week. SE to label runs with quant vs full. CSM to update scorecard.
[19:25] Ethan Morales: Sounds correct. One ask — can Redwood include a change-log for prompt edits so we can track regressions to specific prompt edits?
[19:35] Daniel Park: Yes we'll version prompt sets and include a small diff in the scorecard.
[19:45] Priya Singh: Also please include an aggregate confidence distribution plot so we can see shift.
[19:52] Maya Chen: We'll include that.
[19:58] Laura Kim: Thanks all, I need to drop at 15:10 PT.
[20:05] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up with notes and the link to the updated scorecard.
[20:12] Sofia Alvarez: I'll own meeting notes and share.
[20:20] End of recording.

References shared: helix_pilot_scorecard_2025-08-12.csv (drive), prompt_sets/v2 (drive), compliance-pack/redwood_SOC2_ISO.zip (CRM link).

Action items (captured in transcript): see action_items field.

Quality notes: transcription contains minor name/term errors (e.g., Sam L vs SAML, KV cache sometimes "K V cache").
